newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL sign deal with Gaz de France.
newsitem.headline: MOL sign deal with Gaz de France.

text.p: Hungary's oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL)has signed a long-term deal under which Gaz de France (GdF) will deliver an annual 400 million cubic meters of gas to MOL, the company said on Thursday.
"This contract brings the proportion of non-Russian gas imports close to 15 percent," MOL said in a statement, adding that the contract with GDF was signed on December 16.
Company officials declined to put a value on the deal.
Parallel with this contract, MOL has signed a ten-year delivery agreement with regional gas distributors DEGAZ and EGAZ, the company said.
MOL imported 5.53 billion cubic meters of natural gas in the first nine months of 1996.
Hungary's gas consumption is expected to grow from 10 billion cubic metres to 13 to 14 billion cubic metres a year within 15 years while domestic extraction is forecast to shrink.
At present, some 65 percent of MOL's gas sales come from imports, mostly from Russia.
Although MOL signed a 20-year delivery deal with gas importer Panrusgas, a 50-50 joint venture with Russia's Gazprom RAO, MOL has emphasized the need to diversify gas imports.
In September, MOL signed a 10-year deal with Germany's Ruhrgas AG for the supply of a total five billion cubic meters of gas.
The state privatisation agency APV RT still holds 58.6 percent of MOL, which has a registered capital of 98.4 billion forints.
A further 17 percent stake is expected to be offered by APV in the first half of 1997.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 1,955 forints, up 25.
